correctness.summary: Gheorghiciuc--Ward (2007) gives a uniform fixed-level occupancy approximation with summable total error. Summing it over all substring lengths, controlling the varying window count by the exact increment of the occupancy deficit, and applying Mellin analysis yields the stated n log_d n+n P_d({log_d n})+O_d((log n)^2) expansion. The Mellin transform and Fourier coefficients were independently checked numerically, and the elementary finite sandwich was exhaustively verified for small binary and ternary words.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Strong prior art includes the 2007 uniform kth-level asymptotic, the 2004 exact extremal count and random n^2-scale comparison, the 2020 logarithmic-level profile analysis, and a 2016 public heuristic with the correct coefficient-one n log_d n deficit. The originality claim is restricted to the all-length second-order periodic expansion, its explicit Fourier coefficients/mean, and the finite collision sandwich/additive O(n) extremal comparison. Older trie/suffix-tree analytic results remain a material risk of equivalent implicit coverage.

value.summary: The result resolves the full linear-order correction to the all-length expectation, identifies its digital phase and Fourier spectrum, and quantifies how exceptionally small the binary oscillation is. It upgrades a recent all-length bound and makes a nontrivial global consequence of fixed-level subword-complexity theory explicit.

limitations: The alphabet size d is fixed and the letters are uniform and independent.
The O((log n)^2) remainder uses the 2007 uniform fixed-level approximation.
The next logarithmic-order phase term is not identified.
No extension to nonuniform memoryless or dependent sources is claimed.
No variance or concentration result for D_n is proved.
Older trie/suffix-tree profile literature remains a material residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
